deep.reconstruction: There is no mathematics on this page. It is a German prose page from a history notebook, part of a running narrative on Alexander the Great, continuous with the previous and next pages. Content, in order: (1) Composition of Alexander's army. It numbered 40,000 men. The cavalry was partly Thessalian and partly Thracian. There was also a select mounted bodyguard drawn from the nobility (the Companions) and a foot guard with silver spears (the Argyraspides / hypaspists). (2) In 334 BC Alexander marched into Asia while Darius III held the Persian throne. The Persians had made few preparations but had put Memnon, their best general, in command. (3) All troops were gathered in Asia Minor. Memnon took up position at the river Granicus. Alexander crossed the river at the greatest risk to his life. The narrative continues on the next page with the victory, Lydia, Ephesus, Halicarnassus and Issus. The neat, uniform, schoolroom-style hand and the content suggest lecture or school notes (possibly copied or dictated) rather than Gauss's own working papers. Attribution to Gauss's hand is doubtful, and there is nothing to reconstruct mathematically.
errors: Historical, not mathematical: Memnon was not the supreme commander at the Granicus. He was one of several commanders, and the satraps chose to fight there against his advice to retreat and burn the land.
The figure of 40,000 is a rounded total. Ancient sources give roughly 30,000–43,000 infantry plus 4,500–5,500 cavalry.

The cavalry is described as Thessalian and Thracian. The main heavy cavalry was Macedonian (Companions) and Thessalian, with Thracians and others as lighter contingents. This is a simplification rather than a slip.
The year was evidently corrected to 334, which is the correct date for the crossing into Asia.

checkable.asserts: The Granicus crossing (334 BC) precedes the summer-333 campaign and Issus mentioned on the next page by one year (trivial chronology check; no mathematics on the page).

transcription_corrections: Line 6: the year is written as '3_4' with a '3' inserted above a struck digit, i.e. the intended reading is '334' (the machine's '3{+3+}4').

Line 9: the struck-out word at the start, before 'Memnon', appears to be a short false start such as 'At'/'ab'. It is deleted and does not affect the reading 'aber Memnon den besten Feldherren an die Spitze gestellt'.
